title: Modular KV storage adapter and threadpool modernization
creator: Diego Morales
description: Summary: The serving runtime's KV cache layer and I/O threadpool have accumulated brittle assumptions over multiple patches. This task refactors the KV storage surface into a pluggable adapter interface, consolidates shard lifecycle logic, and modernizes the threadpool used by the request scheduler and prefetch workers. Goals are to reduce cross-cutting locks, make on-disk vs in-memory strategies swappable, and upgrade low-level dependencies (liburing/libaio bindings, jemalloc tuning) to improve tail latency and reduce memory fragmentation. The work touches continuous batching (to avoid stalls during cache rehydration), scheduler admission paths, and the async I/O stack.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a stable KVAdapter interface with two implementations: InMemoryShardAdapter and MMapShardAdapter
No functional regressions in core generation paths (smoke tests + integration harness pass)
Request scheduler no longer holds global shard locks during admission; measured lock contention reduced by >= 60% in synthetic tests
Threadpool upgrade replaces custom blocking-thread pool with bounded async worker pool; median and 95th percentile latency for 512-token requests do not increase
Dependency upgrades completed (libaio -> liburing bindings updated, jemalloc bump) and CI artifacts rebuilt with the new toolchain
Migration plan executed with rolling canary: background rehydrate enabled off-by-default then toggled on for 5% traffic, no increase in error budget
tasks: Design: API surface for KVAdapter and lifecycle (Diego)
Prototype: in-memory adapter with shard pinning behavior (Priya)
Implement: MMapShardAdapter with compacted index layout
Refactor: remove global shard lock from scheduler admission path
Replace: threadpool implementation and wire into prefetch + I/O paths
Benchmark: microbench for lock contention, end-to-end p50/p95/p99
Upgrade deps: update liburing bindings, bump jemalloc, run security scanners
Operational: rollout canary plan and dashboard panels (telemetry tags + trace sampling)
